reason: This study aims to explore whether the proportion of SUID (Sudden Unexpected Infant Death) cases with medical complications during pregnancy differs across maternal prepregnancy body mass index (BMI) levels, using only case data from the NCFRP (National Fatality Review Case Reporting System). The design is a case-only analysis, which means it can identify associations within the case series but cannot establish incidence rates or causal relationships. It builds on existing literature that suggests an increased risk of SUID with maternal obesity but does not specifically address how medical complications during pregnancy relate to prepregnancy BMI in SUID cases.
